papers.title: A DNA Typewriter records the cell lineage history of a mouse, from zygote to late organogenesis.
papers.summary: DNA Typewriter, a sequential molecular recorder, captured mouse cell lineage over ~2 weeks of development. From one embryo, researchers reconstructed a zygote-rooted phylogeny of 1.28 million profiled cells, quantified clonal dominance during gastrulation, and showed siblings share cell types above chance, delivering a lineage-anchored ontogeny of mammalian development.

papers.title: Message in a bottleneck: Nested founder effects from French Polynesia to Rapa Nui and Hawai'i.
papers.summary: Whole-genome sequencing across Polynesia reveals settlement bottlenecks an order of magnitude stronger than in European founder populations. Hawai'i and Rapa Nui, the most bottlenecked, were likely settled by the same voyagers with roots in Mangareva. A FAN1 loss-of-function variant common in eastern Polynesia is absent from gnomAD, enabling actionable genetic testing.

papers.title: Golgi-derived vesicles containing PI(3,4)P(2) drive mitochondrial fusion.
papers.summary: Golgi-derived vesicles enriched in PI(3,4)P2 are recruited to ER- and mitofusin-marked mitochondrial fusion sites. Loss of the PI(3,4)P2-generating kinases PI3K-C2α/β causes mitochondrial fragmentation via impaired fusion, and cardiomyocyte-specific double deletion in mice produces fragmentation and heart failure, revealing phosphoinositide-coded vesicle control of mitochondrial membrane remodeling.

papers.title: The human gut microbiome primes fever after vaccination.
papers.summary: In 171 adults receiving SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines, post-vaccination fever risk correlated with low-grade intestinal inflammation and prevaccine abundance of flagellated Lachnospiraceae and flagellin. Microbiomes from fever-high donors drove flagellin-dependent reactions in gnotobiotic mice, and both murine reactions and human fever risk were modifiable by diet, suggesting microbiome-targeted remedies.

papers.title: Epigenetic aging and transposon dysregulation reflect size-related lifespan compression in dogs.
papers.summary: Using 1640 methylomes from 894 dogs, an epigenetic clock predicted mortality and showed aging runs fastest early in life. Larger and male dogs, which are shorter-lived, age faster molecularly. Sex-dependent methylation concentrated on the X chromosome, while size-associated methylation marked transposable elements, nominating TEs as mediators of size-linked lifespan.

papers.title: The genetic basis for the production of toxic quinolizidine alkaloids in lupins.
papers.summary: The full quinolizidine alkaloid biosynthesis pathway in narrow-leafed lupin was elucidated as 15 enzymatic steps using pathway reconstruction and mutant analysis. Major latex protein-like proteins accelerate spontaneous chemical equilibria, and an oxidoreductase ensures stereoselectivity. Researchers engineered a new low-alkaloid line and identified the causal mutation in an existing one.

papers.title: Targeting CD28 on T lineage malignancies with chimeric antigen receptor T cells.
papers.summary: CD28 is overexpressed on pediatric T-ALL blasts and upregulated in nodal T-follicular helper cell lymphomas. CRISPR-mediated CD28 knockout prevented fratricide in anti-CD28 CAR T cells, which matched anti-CD7 CAR T efficacy while sparing CD8 T cells and NK cells, establishing CD28 as an actionable CAR T target for T-cell malignancies.

papers.title: Pregnancy establishment in cattle without embryonic interferon tau.
papers.summary: Using CRISPR-Cas9 to delete the entire interferon tau (IFNT) locus in cattle, IFNT-null embryos developed normally, elongated typically, prevented luteal regression, established normal placentation, and produced healthy calves. This first direct genetic test overturns the long-standing dogma that embryonic IFNT is indispensable for pregnancy recognition in ruminants.

papers.title: A complex relationship: pre-mRNA 3' processing and transcription termination.
papers.summary: This review examines the coupling between pre-mRNA 3'-end processing and transcription termination at gene ends. Contrary to decades of functional coupling, evidence shows changes in these processes can occur in opposing directions; acknowledging this paradox is presented as necessary for a real understanding of how gene ends are shaped.

papers.title: Introgression catalyzing plumage evolution and speciation in an Asian songbird complex.
papers.summary: Comparing Naumann's thrush, dusky thrush, and red-throated thrush with a chromosome-level genome and 66 resequenced individuals, divergence between the first two was confined to genomic islands overlapping regions introgressed from red-throated thrush. These islands harbor melanin genes (ASIP, OCA2, HERC2) under selection, implicating adaptive introgression in plumage-driven speciation.

papers.title: Serum albumin oxidation and inter-alpha-trypsin-inhibitor heavy chain-4 abundance correlates with the dystropathology in the rat model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
papers.summary: In the DMDmdx rat model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, serum and tissue oxidative protein modifications were elevated across disease stages. Serum albumin thiol oxidation increased consistently with age, while ITIH4 chlorination and abundance correlated with muscle inflammation, identifying both as promising blood-based biomarkers for monitoring dystropathology and treatment response.

papers.title: Functional and Mechanistic Characterization of SARS-CoV-2 NSP15 Reveals Metal-Dependent Regulation and Inhibition by Direct-Binding Small Molecules.
papers.summary: SARS-CoV-2 NSP15 endoribonuclease shows moderate stability and strong metal-ion dependence, with Mn2+ as optimal activator. Direct-binding small molecules inhibited activity with IC50 values of ~8-30 µM, confirmed by SPR and fluorescence quenching. Mutagenesis of catalytic residues and the S294 uridine-specificity pocket defined inhibitor binding, supporting NSP15-directed antiviral design.

papers.title: Chromatin stability safeguards mitochondrial homeostasis and restrains TORC1 signaling.
papers.summary: In yeast, a histone H3K37A mutant promotes histone degradation and hyperactivates TORC1, with cytotoxicity upon TORC1 inhibition driven by deregulated mitochondrial retrograde signaling and defective mitochondrial import. Retrograde inactivation or ROS neutralization prevents toxicity, identifying chromatin stability as an upstream restraint on TORC1 and a guardian of mitochondrial homeostasis.

papers.title: Arbutin as a promising cardioprotective anticancer adjuvant with doxorubicin in solid Ehrlich carcinoma through targeting NEK7-dependent inflammasome/SIRT1/caspase-3/oxidative stress pathways.
papers.summary: In a mouse solid Ehrlich carcinoma model, arbutin reduced tumor weight and volume alone or with doxorubicin, suppressing tumor NLRP3, NEK7, and caspase-1 while increasing caspase-3 and lowering SIRT1. Unlike doxorubicin, arbutin attenuated cardiac inflammation and marker elevation, positioning it as a cardioprotective anticancer adjuvant via NEK7/NLRP3-SIRT1 pathways.

papers.title: PRDX4 ameliorates oxidative stress-induced injury in endometriosis: potential association with PTP1B oxidation and downstream phosphorylation cascades.
papers.summary: PRDX4 was elevated in ectopic endometria of ovarian endometriosis and its overexpression promoted cell migration yet protected stromal cells from H2O2-induced injury, requiring catalytic cysteines Cys124/Cys245 and acting via reduced PTP1B oxidation and downstream phosphorylation. In vivo, PRDX4 promoted ectopic lesion growth, suggesting PRDX4 inhibition as an endometriosis strategy.

papers.title: Structure-Dependent Effects of Lipid Conjugation on Cytosolic Accumulation in Escherichia coli and Mammalian Cells.
papers.summary: Using the CHAMP assay on a systematic lipid-conjugate library in HeLa and E. coli, lipidation showed context-dependent effects: most lipid modifications reduced E. coli cytosolic accumulation, while larger, more hydrophobic conjugates were preferentially internalized by mammalian cells. This offers a permeability-based explanation for the scarcity of lipidated antibacterials with cytosolic targets.

papers.title: FAANGMine Genomic Data Warehouse for Farm Animal Species.
papers.summary: FAANGMine is an InterMine-based data warehouse integrating Functional Annotation of Animal Genomes (FAANG) consortium datasets with genes, variants, QTL and expression for farm animals. It unifies chromatin states, accessibility, architecture, histone marks and CTCF sites with RefSeq, Ensembl, KEGG and other sources, queryable via web tools, an API, and JBrowse browsers.

papers.title: BRD8 deficiency leads to progressive impairment of spermatogenesis in mice.
papers.summary: Germ cell-specific BRD8 knockout mice showed reduced testicular size and sperm counts with progressive spermatogenic defects: spermatid loss followed by later declines in spermatocytes and spermatogonia. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed dysregulated translation-related pathways and meiotic genes plus reduced VEGF signaling in endothelium, defining roles for this epigenetic reader in male fertility.

papers.title: The Case for Kinases: a Phosphorylation Driven Model for Circadian Temperature Compensation in Neurospora crassa.
papers.summary: Using novel casein kinase alleles in Neurospora, a phosphorylation-driven model for circadian temperature compensation emerges: CK1 activity on FRQ decreases with temperature, countered by increasing CKII activity. Quantitative proteomics shows FRQ's phosphorylation landscape is temperature-dependent and altered in compensation mutants, with key compensation-specific domains regulating period length.

papers.title: emb-20 encodes a farnesyl diphosphate synthase in Caenorhabditis elegans.
papers.summary: The C. elegans emb-20(g27) mutant carries a missense mutation in fdps-1, encoding farnesyl diphosphate synthase. Defective prenylation of Rab GTPases (RAB-1, -5, -7, -11) disrupted their organelle localization, impairing cortical granule formation, yolk uptake, and oocyte membrane trafficking, establishing mevalonate-derived prenylation as essential for Rab function in developing oocytes.

papers.title: PNBind: Prediction of Nucleic Acid-Binding Sites Using Protein Structure and Protein Language Models.
papers.summary: PNBind is a multimodal deep learning framework combining ESM protein language models, evolutionary features, and 3D structural geometry via a geometric vector perceptron with invariant point attention to predict nucleic acid-binding sites. Benchmarks on DNA-129/181 and RNA-117/285 datasets show strong performance, with ablations confirming the protein language model backbone dominates.

papers.title: Protein Nanocages as Tunable Stoichiometric Benchmarks for Quantitative SMLM.
papers.summary: Self-assembling protein nanocages displaying 60 or 120 GFP copies were evaluated as stoichiometric calibration standards for quantitative single-molecule localization microscopy. mCitrine-tagged 120-mer nanocages gave localization distributions shifted roughly two-fold versus 60-mers, providing tunable, synthetic benchmarks for STORM copy-number calibration in the moderate-to-high copy range, extensible to other stoichiometries and modalities.

papers.title: Clathrin recruitment and assembly of phosphorylated B cell receptor is impaired in human diffuse large B cell lymphoma.
papers.summary: In a human ABC diffuse large B cell lymphoma model, correlative super-resolution and electron microscopy showed spontaneous surface immunoglobulin clusters on smooth raised membrane domains, but phosphorylated CD79a segregated away from clathrin, surface immunoglobulin, and CD79B. This disengagement likely lets the receptor evade endocytic downregulation, sustaining the constitutive signaling that drives lymphoma proliferation.

papers.title: Dependency Map correlation analysis reveals WDR89 as a genome maintenance factor.
papers.summary: Mining DepMap CRISPR/siRNA screen correlations with curated DNA repair gene sets recovered known genome stability genes and surfaced new candidates, validated by siRNA depletion. WDR89, a novel hit, relocalizes in an ATM-dependent manner after DNA damage, interacts with nucleolar proteins, and its depletion triggers nuclear p53/p21 accumulation and G2/M arrest.

papers.title: Septins regulate cytokinesis and multicellular development in the closest living relatives of animals.
papers.summary: The choanoflagellate Salpingoeca rosetta encodes four animal/fungal-related septins. Disrupting three altered cell size and impaired multicellular rosette development; Sros_septa mutants initiated furrow ingression but frequently failed cytokinesis, yielding enlarged multinucleated cells, with requirements heightened during rosette induction. Tagged Sros_septa localized to cleavage furrows, illuminating septin roles in the animal stem lineage.

papers.title: ATP and α-ketoglutarate link nitrogen availability to TORC1-Npr1 signaling in yeast.
papers.summary: TORC1-Npr1 signaling activates upon glucose starvation only under specific nitrogen conditions, driven by increased ATP from stimulated respiration. In proline-grown cells, α-ketoglutarate catabolism fuels this respiration, while high α-ketoglutarate levels inhibit activation. Ammonium assimilation lowers α-ketoglutarate and sustains ATP production, identifying both metabolites as determinants of TORC1-Npr1 nitrogen signaling.

papers.title: Genomic inbreeding and selection signatures analyses in the Doberman Pinscher breed.
papers.summary: Analyzing 3,226 Doberman Pinschers (216,184 SNPs), genomic inbreeding was high (mean FROH 0.42) with recent-inbreeding runs of homozygosity concentrated on CFA2, CFA3, and CFA31. Haplotype-based selection scans and breed comparisons against Labrador Retrievers highlighted genes enriched for developmental and neurodevelopmental pathways, a genomic resource for breed health management.

papers.title: A modular toolkit for theophylline-dependent synthetic auxotrophs via riboswitch-gated essential genes.
papers.summary: Inserting theophylline-responsive riboswitches upstream of 29 essential E. coli genes created ligand-dependent synthetic auxotrophs: 19 targets showed ligand-dependent growth and 18 yielded stringent live-die strains with escape frequencies of 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻⁶ or below detection. The modular, low-cost design enables rapid (<1 week) construction of genetically encoded biocontainment systems.

papers.title: A catalog of mRNAs transferred from males to females during mating in Drosophila arizonae and D. mojavensis.
papers.summary: RNA-seq of female reproductive tracts after heterospecific crosses cataloged 270 candidate male-derived mRNAs in Drosophila arizonae and D. mojavensis, originating from testes, seminal vesicles, and accessory glands. Ribosomal protein enrichment suggests translational roles in females, and GFP-tagged sperm tracking showed transferred sperm trapped in the insemination reaction mass, possibly releasing RNA.

papers.title: A membrane-free spot-plating protocol for Agrobacterium-mediated transformation of diverse yeasts.
papers.summary: A simplified Agrobacterium-mediated transformation protocol for yeasts eliminates membrane filters by centrifuging cells and spot-plating pellets onto induction medium, cutting hands-on time to 15 minutes. In Rhodotorula toruloides it raised efficiency 66% to 2,500 transformants per 10⁶ cells, and it worked across seven ascomycete species including one never transformed before.

papers.title: Identification of shared diagnostic biomarkers and immune-related mechanisms between sepsis and thoracic aortic aneurysm based on integrated bioinformatics and machine learning approaches.
papers.summary: Integrating sepsis and thoracic aortic aneurysm transcriptomes identified 193 shared differentially expressed genes enriched in T cell activation, Th17 differentiation, and oxidative stress. Machine learning selected five candidates (ARG1, IL18R1, LIX1L, TRIM32, PRKCH); in LPS-treated vascular smooth muscle cells, ARG1 and IL18R1 rose while LIX1L fell, supporting shared immune mechanisms.

papers.title: Functional characterization of neutrophils in patients with multiple myeloma.
papers.summary: In a Zambian cohort of 30 multiple myeloma patients and 42 controls, neutrophil phagocytosis (45.0% vs 75.9%) and reactive oxygen species production (44.7% vs 74.9%) were significantly impaired in patients, independent of age, sex, or neutrophil count, demonstrating qualitative neutrophil dysfunction likely contributing to infection risk in multiple myeloma.

papers.title: Temporal and stimulus-specific transcriptional responses of maize to a biostimulant mixture of quillaja extract and fulvic acid.
papers.summary: RNA-seq of maize leaves at 3 and 27 hours after biostimulant application showed dynamic, stimulus-specific responses. Fulvic acid plus quillaja extract induced broader early hormone, ion transport, and transcription factor activation, later emphasizing signaling integration and secondary metabolism, while fulvic acid alone sustained metabolic, redox, and regulatory networks—guiding biostimulant design.

papers.title: Dual targeting of EGFR signaling and microtubule dynamics enhances replication-associated cellular stress and suppresses tumor growth in gefitinib-resistant non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.summary: In gefitinib-resistant NSCLC cells, mebendazole plus gefitinib reduced viability to 37.7% versus minimal effect of gefitinib alone, inducing single- and double-strand DNA breaks and γ-H2AX activation indicative of replication stress. In vivo, the combination prolonged tumor doubling time from 6.2 to 25 days without substantial toxicity, supporting adjuvant repurposing.

papers.title: Research on precise segmentation model of thyroid nodules based on deep learning.
papers.summary: A ResNet34-enhanced deep learning model for thyroid nodule ultrasound segmentation was benchmarked on TN3K and DDTI datasets, with ImageNet pretraining and feature pyramid integration delivering the best performance (Res34-PAN: IoU 0.8778, F1 0.9349 on DDTI). The work addresses ambiguous nodule boundaries and inter-observer variability in ultrasound-based diagnosis.

papers.title: Surfactant protein A (SP-A) alleviates acute kidney injury by reducing macrophage recruitment and M1 polarization.
papers.summary: In a mouse renal ischemia model, surfactant protein A activation preserved renal function, reduced creatinine and urea nitrogen, and attenuated tissue damage by suppressing CD11b+F4/80+ macrophage infiltration, shifting polarization from M1 toward M2, and inhibiting NF-κB signaling, positioning SP-A as a promising therapeutic target for acute kidney injury.

papers.title: A Homozygous ALCAM-CBLB Deletion at 3q13.11-q13.12 Defines a Candidate Novel Oculo-Skeletal-Immune Contiguous Gene Deletion Syndrome.
papers.summary: A consanguineous boy with ocular, craniofacial, skeletal, cardiac, and immune abnormalities carried a 2.5-Mb homozygous 3q13.11-q13.12 deletion removing ALCAM and CBLB, with confirmed absent expression. Animal models support the phenotype components, and this first reported combined homozygous deletion defines a candidate novel oculo-skeletal-immune contiguous gene deletion syndrome.

papers.title: Inducible tristetraprolin suppresses malignant phenotypes and directly targets glucosaminyl (N-acetyl) transferase 3 in lung cancer cells.
papers.summary: Using a doxycycline-inducible TTP knock-in in H460 lung cancer cells, induced TTP suppressed clonogenicity, proliferation, invasion, and migration. GCNT3 emerged as a direct TTP target: TTP bound GCNT3 and reduced its expression, GCNT3 knockdown attenuated invasion, and GCNT3 re-expression restored malignant behaviors, defining a post-transcriptional axis in lung cancer progression.

papers.title: Kinetics and mechanisms in lipopolysaccharide-induced neuroinflammation: a framework for phytochemicals screening.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes LPS-induced neuroinflammation models used for phytochemical screening, covering in vitro microglial systems, dosing (100 ng/mL to 1 µg/mL), kinetics, and in vivo paradigms. Heterogeneity in LPS provenance and endpoints undermines comparability; the authors propose a kinetics- and mechanism-informed framework treating LPS as a controlled inflammatory trigger, not a disease surrogate.

papers.title: Targeting the IRE1α/XBP1 pathway in type 2 diabetes mellitus: from ER stress signaling to therapeutic opportunity.
papers.summary: This review examines the IRE1α/XBP1 branch of the unfolded protein response in type 2 diabetes: adaptive XBP1 signaling expands ER capacity, while chronic IRE1α activation drives RIDD, JNK, and NLRP3 deleterious effects. Its extensive crosstalk with metabolic and inflammatory pathways makes the pathway an attractive disease-modifying therapeutic target in T2DM.

papers.title: Deoxynivalenol-induced cellular signal transduction: research progress on toxicological effects, molecular mechanisms, and biological intervention strategies.
papers.summary: This review summarizes deoxynivalenol (DON) mycotoxin toxicity across intestinal, immune, nervous, and reproductive systems, triggered by the ribotoxic stress response and amplified via MAPK, PI3K/Akt/mTOR, NF-κB, and other crosstalk into ROS, ER stress, apoptosis, and ferroptosis. Probiotic and postbiotic interventions are appraised, with current bottlenecks and future directions outlined.

papers.title: Expression profiling of the gibberellin 2-oxidase gene CsGA2ox2 (Cucumis sativus L.) reveals stage- and tissue-specific transcript accumulation during fruit development.
papers.summary: CsGA2ox2, a gibberellin 2-oxidase catabolizing bioactive gibberellins in cucumber, showed stage- and tissue-specific transcript accumulation during fruit development: low early, peaking by 21 days after pollination, and consistently higher in pulp than pericarp. Findings are descriptive and computational, providing a foundation for functional studies of GA catabolism in cucurbit fruit.

papers.title: Spatio-temporal expression of E-cadherin mediates trophoblast lineage transitions during human placentation.
papers.summary: E-cadherin expression fluctuates dynamically across human trophoblast lineages: upregulated for cytotrophoblast aggregation, then downregulated for syncytial fusion along the villous pathway; transiently reduced for epithelial-to-mesenchymal invasion, then restored in endovascular trophoblasts. Dysregulation is evident in preeclampsia and fetal growth restriction, with soluble E-cadherin proposed as a biomarker candidate for defective placentation.

papers.title: Oral administration of ultrafine-grained Astragalus membranaceus enhances peripheral immunity in weaned black Xiangdong goats by upregulating the complement regulator C4bp and immunoglobulin responses.
papers.summary: In weaned black Xiangdong goats, oral ultrafine-grained Astragalus membranaceus (10 g/day, days 43-78) significantly increased serum C4bp, hepatic C4bp mRNA, and serum IgM without changing IgA, IgG, or inflammatory cytokines, and was independently associated with C4bp, suggesting engagement of complement regulatory pathways and potential post-weaning immune support.

papers.title: Molecular Characterization of vanA and bla(TEM) Mutant Genes in Enterococcus faecalis: In silico and in vitro investigation of Sitagliptin as a potential Resistance Modulator.
papers.summary: Among 350 Iraqi clinical samples, 83 Enterococcus faecalis isolates carried vanA and blaTEM resistance genes with identified SNPs. Sitagliptin altered resistance gene expression—raising vanA 3.66-fold and lowering blaTEM to 0.75-fold—and showed synergy with amoxicillin in checkerboard assays, supporting investigation as an antibiotic-resistance-modifying adjunct rather than a bactericidal agent.

papers.title: Expression and functional characterisation of the zinc-dependent metalloprotease LIC11568 from Leptospira interrogans reveals collagenolytic activity.
papers.summary: The Leptospira interrogans LIC11568 protein, an M23 metalloprotease with LysM domains and a signal peptide, was produced by cell-free synthesis and confirmed by MALDI-TOF. It degraded type I collagen time-dependently, peaking at pH 8.0 and 37°C, with zinc-dependent activity inhibited by 1,10-phenanthroline—its first biochemical characterization as a collagenolytic virulence candidate.

papers.title: Mechanometabolic endothelial senescence as a translational framework for cardiometabolic vascular disease and vascular ageing.
papers.summary: This review proposes 'mechanometabolic endothelial senescence' as a framework linking local hemodynamic vulnerability with systemic cardiometabolic load: low or oscillatory shear, matrix stiffness, hyperglycemia, and inflammation converge on DNA damage, p53/p21, NAD⁺-sirtuin decline, and mitochondrial dysfunction. It offers a staged validation strategy and positions senescence as a disease amplifier, not universal primary cause.
